After surviving the darkness of the sea, a warrior returns to the people she once left behind. Together, they rebuild more than a ship—they rebuild hope, purpose, and the courage to begin again. But their journey is far from over.

Inspired by the spirit of sea shanties and cinematic maritime folk music, “Mother Told Me” carries the voices, storms, memories, and determination of those who refuse to surrender to the sea.

This music video continues the story from the previous chapter, and the story will continue in future videos. Subscribe to the channel, turn on notifications, and follow Wolfskald so you don’t miss the next part.

Frost in my hair
I watched the dark sea
Take all I held dear

My bones were sore
Still I kept rowing
Toward the shore

Hear the drowned bell
Toll beneath the foam
Some will return
Some never come home

Hold to the rail
Hold to your name
The sea cannot drown
An undying flame

My mother told me
Daughter, stand tall
My mother told me
Storms rise and fall

My mother told me
Sing through the night
My mother told me
We’ll see dawn’s first light

Lanterns were fading
One by one
The mast was breaking
But we carried on

The old gods were silent
Cold in the spray
I gave all my fear
To the sea that day

Hear the drowned bell
Toll beneath the foam
Some will return
Some never come home

Hold to the rail
Hold to your name
The sea cannot drown
An undying flame

My mother told me
Daughter, stand tall
My mother told me
Storms rise and fall

My mother told me
Sing through the night
My mother told me
We’ll see dawn’s first light

Let the deep drums thunder
Let the ancient war cry rise
Carry the fallen’s final words
Beyond the northern skies

If I am bound to sink
I’ll face the deep with pride
With every sacred vow I made
Still burning deep inside

ABOUT POLYPHONIC FACE

Polyphonic Face was born from an idea I originally called “Schrödinger’s Heart.”

Sometimes we avoid an answer because, as long as we don't look, every possibility can still exist. The message remains unopened. The doors remain closed. Two futures run in parallel.

But not choosing is still a decision.

This song is about that strange space between knowing and not knowing, holding on and letting go, staying and leaving. And about the moment when we finally decide to open the message, leave the hallway and walk toward whatever comes next.
